Document.description: A whole deployment: one node or an HA pair.

backup.description: Scheduled backups of the node bundle.

dns.description: Recursive DNS for the served networks.

management.description: Which network is management, and the anti-lockout switch.

networks.description: Layer-2 segments, keyed by network name (also the interface name).

objects.description: Named address and port sets, referenced from rules as `@name`.

ports.description: Per node: port role name to the hardware it is bound to.

provider_options.description:
Per-provider passthrough settings, keyed by provider name (#143):
set straight in that provider's own configuration, for what the
rest of the document doesn't cover. Keys Sparewall sets itself are
refused, the provider's config test checks the rest, and options
for a provider not in use are ignored with a warning.

kea.description: Kea's Dhcp4 settings, merged into the rendered Dhcp4 object, as in Kea's own configuration (client-classes, option-def, global option-data, timers). Under networks.<network>, settings merged into that DHCP network's subnet; its option-data is added to Sparewall's own.

unbound.description: Unbound settings by clause: server (options for its server: clause; a list gives an option more than once), and forward-zone and stub-zone (lists of clauses, each with a name). Values are written as given, so quote them where Unbound wants quotes.

raw.description: Raw nft statements placed at named hook points.

schema.description:
The oldest schema revision that reads this document: the newest
revision among the fields it uses. Set when the document is
applied; a release refuses one newer than it reads.

vpn_clients.description:
WireGuard tunnels this node connects to as a client, of a service
it does not run (a VPN provider, a cloud host, another
organisation's hub): chosen networks' traffic leaves through the
tunnel instead of the WAN (#149).

zones.description: Named groups of networks. `self` is built in and cannot be defined.

Document.title: Sparewall configuration document

ca.description:
PEM of the CA that signs the directory's TLS certificate, for a
private CA (default: the system trust store).

eab.description: External Account Binding key ID and secret reference.

credentials.description:
Secret reference, `secret:<name>`. For `rfc2136`, the TSIG key as
`algorithm:name:secret`; for lego, the provider's credentials as
`KEY=value` lines.

options.description:
For `rfc2136`, `server` (host[:port]) and `zone`; for lego, the
provider's other environment variables (`GCE_PROJECT`), and lego's
own (`LEGO_DNS_RESOLVERS`).

provider.description:
`rfc2136` (built in), or a lego provider code such as `gcloud`,
`cloudflare` or `route53` (https://go-acme.github.io/lego/dns/).

credentials.description: Secret reference for repository credentials (not the password).

retention.description:
What the repository keeps of this node's snapshots: after each
successful send the node runs `restic forget` on its own snapshots
(`--host <node> --tag sparewall`) with these keep rules, restic's own
names. Without it, a repository keeps `hourly: 48, daily: 30,
weekly: 12, monthly: 24`; `enabled: false` keeps everything (#140).

members.description: Member NICs, each a permanent MAC address or udev path.

Document.Cidr.description: IPv4 address with prefix length, e.g. 192.0.2.1/24

conntrack.description: Connection-tracking sizing, identical on both nodes.

hold.description:
Stage beside the gateway this replaces: everything runs, but no
gateway address is claimed (VRRP instances held in FAULT, or not
installed standalone) and DHCP offers nothing. Set false to cut over.

nodes.description:
One node name (standalone) or two (an HA pair). Each is also that
node's hostname: up to 31 lowercase letters, digits and '-',
starting with a letter and not ending with '-'.

sync_keys.description: Each node's sync-tunnel WireGuard public key, from `sparewall status`.

sync_network.description: The network with role `sync` that carries the pair's WireGuard tunnel.

sync_port.description: UDP port of the sync tunnel.

Document.Dhcp.description: DHCPv4: service-wide settings plus one entry per served network.

ha.description: HA mode for a pair. Default `hot-standby`.

ping_check.description:
Ping an address before offering it, and skip it if something
answers: a host still using it without a lease here (after a
restore, or when replacing another DHCP server). Default true; turn
it off on networks that filter ICMP echo.

provider.description: Implementation: `kea` (the default). `networkd` is not built yet.

lease_time.description: Lease time in seconds for this network.

options.description: Options; router, DNS and NTP default to the gateway address.

ping_check.description: Ping before offering on this network (default: `dhcp.ping_check`).

dynamic.description:
Names kept pointing at the site's public address as it changes
(#316), by a name of your own: dynamic DNS. Independent of the
resolver: `enabled` turns only the resolver on and off.

filters.description:
Blocklists the firewall's resolver applies to the networks that
want them (#74), by a name of your own: a blocked name gets
NXDOMAIN, with its subdomains.

forwarders.description: Forward to these servers instead of recursing.

intercept.description:
Networks whose DNS queries go to the resolver the site chose,
whatever server a client asks (#73), by network name: the
firewall's own resolver there, or `to`.

networks.description: Networks to serve; default every network with DHCP.

records.description: Extra local A records, name to address.

tls_ca.description:
PEM of a CA that signs a TLS forwarder's certificate, for a private
resolver: trusted for every TLS forwarder, besides the system
trust store.

tls_forwarders.description:
Forward over TLS instead (#356), by a name of your own: each
forwarder's certificate is verified against its `name`, and there
is no fallback to plain DNS. In place of `forwarders`.

allow.description: Names never blocked, with their subdomains, whatever the lists say.

block.description: Names blocked whatever the lists say.

lists.description:
Blocklists to fetch, by URL: hosts files, one name per line, or
adblock-style `||name^` lines. Fetched again every `refresh`; the
last good copy is kept.

networks.description:
Networks whose queries it filters. The firewall's resolver must
serve them.

refresh.description:
How often the lists are fetched (`24h`, `6h`, `1d`). Default `24h`;
at least `1h`.

Document.DnsIntercept.description: How a network's DNS queries are intercepted (`dns.intercept.<network>`).

block_dot.description:
Refuse DNS over TLS (TCP 853) from the network, so clients fall back
to plain DNS. Default true. DNS over HTTPS can't be told apart by
its port.

to.description:
Send them to this resolver instead of the firewall's own, e.g. a
Pi-hole. Queries over IPv6 are then refused, so clients ask over
IPv4.

Document.DnsTlsForwarder.description: A resolver forwarded to over TLS (`dns.tls_forwarders.<name>`, #356).

name.description:
The name its certificate is verified against, e.g.
`dns.quad9.net`.

Document.DynamicDns.description:
Dynamic DNS (`dns.dynamic.<name>`): names a provider keeps at the
WAN's address. In a pair, only the master sends updates.

credentials.description:
`secret:<name>`, the provider's credentials as `KEY=value` lines:
`DYNDNS2_USERNAME` and `DYNDNS2_PASSWORD`; `CF_DNS_API_TOKEN`
(lego's name, so one secret can serve both); `DUCKDNS_TOKEN`
(lego's too).

discover.description:
Ask this service for the public IPv4 address instead of taking the
WAN's, for a WAN behind carrier-grade NAT or another router: a URL
that answers with the address alone, e.g. `https://api.ipify.org`.

ipv6.description: Keep the names' AAAA records at the WAN's global IPv6 address too.

names.description: The names to keep current, e.g. `vpn.example.org`.

network.description:
The WAN network whose address the names get (default: the only
WAN).

options.description:
Provider settings. `server`: the update URL for `dyndns2`
(required, e.g. `https://dynupdate.no-ip.com/nic/update`), or a
compatible service's API for the others. `zone`: the Cloudflare
zone (default: found from the names).

provider.description:
`dyndns2` (Dyn, No-IP and the many services that speak its
protocol), `cloudflare` or `duckdns`.

network.description: The network whose addresses fill the set.

source.description: `address` for the node's own address, `prefix` for the subnet.

dst.description: Original destination; default any address of the arriving zone.

from.description: Zone the connections arrive from. Default `wan`.

hairpin.description:
Inside zones whose clients may also use the forward by its outside
address (NAT reflection), e.g. `[users]`. Needs `dst`. Clients on
the server's own network are also source-NATed to the firewall's
address there, so that replies come back through it.

connections.description: Record connection start/end with NAT mappings.

group.description: nflog group used for rule logging. Default 0.

anti_lockout.description:
Always accept SSH and HTTPS from the management network to `self`.
Only an `admin` may turn this off.

sources.description:
Who on the management network reaches SSH and HTTPS through the
anti-lockout rule: addresses, prefixes, ranges or `@objects`, of
either family. Each family is admitted from the sources it names,
IPv6 where the management network has it (schema revision 6). Unset,
every host there does. Worth setting when the management network is
also an ordinary one, such as a two-NIC box's LAN (#177).

web.description:
Serve the web UI and the HTTP API (`sparewall-httpd`) on the HTTPS
port, next to the health endpoints. Off by default; reached only
where HTTPS is, the management network.

password.description:
Also accept the `admin` password (`sparewall passwd`) over SSH, not
only keys. Off by default: the password is the console's
break-glass path.

Document.Match.description:
A match value: a scalar, a list, or an `@object` reference. An IPv6
address in one needs schema revision 5 (`x-since-ipv6`): earlier
releases read only IPv4 there.

mode.description:
`external`: `/metrics` answers the management network without a
token, for an external Prometheus. `local`: each node also keeps
its own history in a local Prometheus, which the API queries
(`org.sparewall.Metrics`); `/metrics` needs a token, as it does
without a `metrics` section. `off`: not served.

retention.description:
With `mode: local`, how long history is kept, in Prometheus's units
(`15d`, `12h`, `1y`). Default `15d`.

retention_size.description:
With `mode: local`, the most history may take on disk (`512MB`,
`2GB`): past it, the oldest goes first, whatever `retention` says.
Default `1GB`.

addresses.description: Each node's own address on this network, in CIDR form.

cake.description: WAN shaping with CAKE, e.g. `{ egress: 900mbit }`.

dhcp_client.description: Obtain this node's address by DHCP (WAN or management only).

dns.description: Upstream DNS servers learned statically on this network.

extra_vips.description:
More addresses that move with the gateway address (in its VRRP
instance in a pair; static standalone), for forwards and SNAT, e.g.
a mail server's public address. In the gateway address's subnet.

gateway.description:
Upstream gateway (default route) for a static WAN or a management
network with its own upstream.

ipv6.description:
IPv6 on this network (#211). Unset, the network has link-local
IPv6 addresses only, and routes none. Not on the sync network
(`x-except-roles`, for editors).

lldp.description: Emit and receive LLDP on this network. Default true on untagged ports.

port.description: The port role this network rides on.

role.description: What the network is for. Default `service`.

vip.description:
The gateway address clients use. Moved by VRRP in a pair, a plain
static address on a standalone node.

vlan.description: 802.1Q VLAN ID; omit for the untagged network of a port.

vmac.description:
On a pair's WAN with private node addresses and a static block:
carry the gateway addresses and the public route behind the VRRP
virtual MAC (`00:00:5e:00:01:<vrid>`), so a handover changes no MAC
the upstream sees (the default). `false` puts them on the nodes'
own MACs, for an upstream that limits the MACs it learns on a port.
Not `cluster.vrrp.use_vmac`, keepalived's own virtual MAC for the
other networks' instances.

vrid.description: VRRP virtual router ID (1-255), unique across the deployment.

Document.NetworkIpv6.description:
How a network gets its IPv6 addresses. Which fields apply depends on
`mode` and on the network's role: each field's `x-modes` lists the
modes it applies to, and `x-role` the networks: `wan`, or `inside`
(neither a WAN nor the sync network), for editors (the web UI shows a
field only where it applies).

addresses.description: `static` on a standalone node's WAN: its own address, in `prefix`.

dns.description:
On an inside network: the resolvers its router advertisements
name (RDNSS), in place of the node, whatever DHCPv4 hands out; an
empty list names none. Unset, they name the node where DHCPv4
does, and none otherwise.

gateway.description:
`static` on a WAN: the upstream router, in `prefix` or link-local
(`fe80::1`).

mode.description:
On a WAN: `dhcpv6` (an address by DHCPv6 or SLAAC, as the
upstream's router advertisements say, and a delegated prefix for
the inside networks), `ra` (an address by SLAAC only, no delegated
prefix) or `static`. On another network: `delegated` (a /64 of the
WAN's delegated prefix) or `static`.

prefix.description:
`static`: the network's prefix. A /64 on an inside network; on a
WAN, the upstream link's prefix.

prefix_length.description:
`dhcpv6`: the length of the prefix to ask the ISP to delegate, 48
to 64. Default 56. The ISP may delegate another.

subnet_id.description:
`delegated`: which /64 of the delegated prefix this network takes,
counting from 0 (a /56 has 256). Unique among the networks.

vip.description:
`static` on a pair's WAN: the address the ISP routes the site to,
which moves with the gateway (the nodes have no IPv6 address of
their own there).

servers.description:
Upstream servers or pools, by host name or address (a name with
`pool` in it is used as a pool).

Document.Object.description: A named set: static elements, or a dynamic set filled by networkd.

dynamic.description:
Fill from a network's addresses instead (`ipv4` and `ipv6`): the
node's own, or the network's prefix.

elements.description:
Static elements: addresses, prefixes or ranges for `ipv4` and
`ipv6`, ports or ranges for `port`.

suffixes.description:
`ipv6`: hosts in a network's IPv6 prefix, by the network and their
suffix, the address's last 64 bits (`users: ["::20"]`). They follow
the prefix, so a rule for a host survives the ISP renumbering a
delegated one (schema revision 6). Each host configures its own
address, with that suffix.

Document.Policy.description: Policy for traffic from one zone to another.

action.description: What happens to traffic no rule matched.

log.description: Log traffic that reaches the default action.

nat.description: Source NAT applied to this zone pair.

Document.Port.description: What a port role is bound to on one node.

mtu.description: MTU of the port (VLAN networks may set their own, no larger).

nic.description:
One NIC, matched by permanent MAC address (`52:54:00:aa:00:01`) or by
udev path (`pci-0000:01:00.0`).

offload.description: NIC offload overrides for misbehaving drivers.

Document.RawEntry.description: A raw nft statement placed at a hook point.

nft.description: The nft statement, without a trailing comment.

order.description: Position among raw entries at the same point.

oneOf.description: Prerouting at raw priority (`notrack`, early drops).
Forward, before zone dispatch (global blocks, MSS clamping).
Postrouting at source-NAT priority (custom SNAT, marks).

ca.description:
syslog only: PEM of the CA that signs the collector's certificate,
for a private CA (default: the system trust store).

certificate.description:
syslog only, with `tls`: this node's client certificate for a
collector that requires one (RELP over TLS always does), as a
secret reference, `secret:<name>`: the private key and the
certificate (with any intermediates), PEM, in one secret.

destination.description:
For journal-upload, a URL or `host:port`. For syslog, `host` or
`host:port`; the port defaults to 514 (`udp`, `tcp`), 6514 (`tcp`
with `tls`) or 2514 (`relp`).

protocol.description:
syslog only: `udp` (the default; messages can be lost), `tcp`, or
`relp` (acknowledged delivery).

provider.description:
`journal-upload` (the default): systemd-journal-upload to a
systemd-journal-remote collector. `syslog`: rsyslog, to a syslog
collector (RFC 5424), over `protocol`.

tls.description:
Encrypt, and check the collector's certificate: its name must be
the destination's host. syslog: with `tcp` or `relp`.

hostname.description: Hostname to hand out (and publish in local DNS).

Document.Retention.description:
restic's keep rules (`restic forget --keep-*`): a snapshot is kept if
any rule keeps it.

hourly.description: The newest snapshot of each of the last N hours (`--keep-hourly`).

action.description: What to do with matching packets.

dport.description: Destination port(s): a number, `low-high`, a list, or `@object`.

order.description: Position within the zone pair; leave gaps (100, 200, ...).

proto.description:
`tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `icmpv6` or another protocol name nft knows.
`icmp` is IPv4's and `icmpv6` IPv6's, so either limits the rule to
its family.

sport.description: Source port(s): a number, `low-high`, a list, or `@object`.

src.description:
Source: an address, a prefix, a range, a list of them, or
`@object`, of either family. The rule applies to the families its
addresses (and `proto`) allow: with only IPv4 ones, to IPv4 only.

check.description:
Check the channel for a newer image every few hours, and log when
one appears (on by default). `false` keeps the node from contacting
the registry on its own, for an air-gapped site; `sparewall upgrade
--check` still asks when run.

mode.description:
`manual` (the default): upgrades run when asked for, with
`sparewall upgrade`. `windowed`: the pair's master (or a standalone
node) upgrades by itself when `window` opens and the channel offers
a newer image, through the same health-gated sequence (#84).

window.description:
When a scheduled upgrade may start: a systemd calendar expression
(`Sun *-*-* 03:00`), in the node's time zone (UTC unless set).
Required with `mode: windowed`.

window_minutes.description:
How many minutes after the window opens an upgrade may still start
(default 60).

client_allowed_ips.description: Networks routed through the tunnel in client configs; default all.

dns.description: DNS servers pushed in client configs.

endpoint.description: Public name or address clients connect to.

extra_ports.description:
More UDP ports clients may use from networks that block the listen
port, e.g. `[53, 443]`: redirected to it on the WAN gateway address.

zone.description: The zone the tunnel interface belongs to.

addresses.description: The tunnel addresses the service assigned.

dns.description:
DNS servers DHCP hands to the routed networks, unless a network
sets its own (`dhcp.<network>.options.dns`): usually the service's
resolvers, which are reached through the tunnel.

private_key.description:
This node's private key, as the service issued it: a cluster
secret, `secret:<name>` (in a pair both nodes are the same client).

zone.description:
The zone the tunnel interface belongs to: policies from the routed
networks' zones to it let their traffic through.

endpoint.description: `host:port`, an address or a DNS name.

keepalive.description:
Seconds between keepalives (default 25): they keep the service's
NAT mapping open, and let health tell a dead tunnel.

preshared_key.description: A preshared key, if the service issued one: `secret:<name>`.

kill_switch.description:
While the tunnel is down, drop these networks' traffic to the WAN
rather than let it leave there (default true).

networks.description:
The networks whose traffic to anywhere but this node's own
networks leaves through the tunnel. The node's own traffic, and
every other network's, keeps the WAN.

addresses.description:
The peer's tunnel address, and for a site-to-site peer the networks
behind it, which are routed through the tunnel.

endpoint.description:
`host:port`, an address or a DNS name: a site-to-site peer, which
this node connects to as well as accepting it. A name is resolved
again while the peer does not answer.

keepalive.description:
Seconds between keepalives to the peer (WireGuard's
`PersistentKeepalive`): it keeps a NAT mapping open, and keeps a
site-to-site tunnel up, so that after a failover the new master
starts it again within this time.

preshared_key.description:
WireGuard preshared key, a cluster secret: `secret:<name>`. The
client must be configured with the same key (`wg genpsk`).

advert_interval_cs.description: Advertisement interval in centiseconds (VRRPv3). Default 100 (1 s).

preempt_delay_s.description:
Fail back by itself: the node with the higher priority takes the
gateway addresses back once it has been up and eligible for this
many seconds (1-1000). Unset (the default), the pair never
preempts, so it cannot bounce while that node flaps; move the
addresses with `sparewall failover` instead. The delay is then the
only protection against flapping.

priority.description: VRRP priority per node; give the larger node the higher value.

unicast.description: Send adverts unicast to the peer instead of multicast.

Error.description: A Varlink error: its name and parameters, and a message in words. The HTTP status follows the error (422 ValidationFailed, 409 Conflict, NotPending and ConfirmTimeout, 401 PermissionDenied without credentials and 403 with them, 404 NotFound, MethodNotFound and InterfaceNotFound, 503 PeerUnreachable and ServiceUnavailable, 400 NotSupported, InvalidParameter and malformed calls, 500 the rest; the gateway's own: 502 Unavailable, 404 NotFound, 405 MethodNotAllowed, 413 TooLarge).

parameters.description: `role` is `none` on a connection not bound to a token.
A service the call needs is not answering (the local Prometheus, for `org.sparewall.Metrics`).

errors.description: Each problem as one line, `path: message`.

issues.description: The same problems, each with its place in the document (#305). Absent from nodes older than 0.8.0.

path.description: The place as the validator names it: names joined by `.`, and `[n]` for a list index, e.g. `networks.lan.dhcp.ranges[0]`. A name that would not read back as itself (holding a `.`, `[`, `]`, a quote or a `\`, with whitespace at either end, or empty) is quoted with `'`, a `'` or `\` inside escaped with `\`; policy keys always are: `policy.'users->wan'.rules.'allow.web'`. Null for a problem with no place in the document.

pointer.description: The same place as an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, e.g. `/networks/lan/dhcp/ranges/0`, for marking the field. It may name a field the document leaves out (a required one). Null when `path` is.

parameters.description: Calls are POST; files are GET.
No call or file has this path.
The request body is over the gateway's limit.
The coordinator did not answer the gateway.
Method is expected to be called with 'more' set to true, but wasn't.
Method is expected to be called with 'upgrade' set to true, but wasn't.
The requested interface was not found.

interface.description: The interface that was not found.

parameters.description: One of the passed parameters is invalid.
The requested method was not found.

method.description: The method that was not found.

parameters.description: The interface defines the requested method, but the service does not implement it.

method.description: The method that is not implemented.

parameters.description: Client is denied access.

expires.description: Unix time it expires, if ever.

locked.description: No password: the user cannot log in.

org.sparewall.Diagnostics.LogEntry.description: One journal entry of Sparewall's own units.

fields.description: The entry's other fields, such as an upgrade's `F_STEP` and `F_DETAIL` or a rule hit's `F_RULE`; not the journal's own (`_PID`, `__CURSOR` and the like).

time.description: When it was logged (RFC 3339, in microseconds).

unit.description: The unit it came from (`sparewalld.service`), or `selinux` for a denial of the coordinator's domain.

org.sparewall.Diagnostics.Neighbour.description: An entry of the neighbour table (ARP, NDP).

network.description: The network the interface carries, if the document has it.

router.description: It says it is a router (IPv6).

org.sparewall.Diagnostics.Route.description: A route, from any table but the local one.

expires.description: Seconds left, for one that expires.

network.description: The network the interface carries, if the document has it.

org.sparewall.Diagnostics.RuleHit.description: A hit of a rule, policy default or forward with `log: true`.

in_iface.description: The interfaces it came in on and was going out of.

time.description: When it was logged (RFC 3339, in microseconds).

hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical document (empty for bootstrap).

session.description: A browser session from org.sparewall.Auth.Login. Requests with it must also carry the X-Sparewall-Request header.
session.name: sparewall_session

info.description: The Sparewall coordinator's Varlink interfaces over HTTPS, as sparewall-httpd serves them. Each call is checked against the role of the caller's API token or session (x-sparewall-role).
info.title: Sparewall

post.description: Bind this connection to a token (an API token or a session's): later calls act with its role. Needed first on the restricted socket.
post.summary: Bind this connection to a token (an API token or a session's): later calls act with its role.

post.description: Create an API token with `role`, expiring after `expires_days` if given. The token is shown once.

token.description: Shown once; only its hash is kept.

post.summary: Create an API token with `role`, expiring after `expires_days` if given.

post.description: API tokens (never their values).
post.summary: API tokens (never their values).

post.description: Users and their roles, `admin` first.
post.summary: Users and their roles, `admin` first.

post.description: Check a user's password and open a session of 12 hours; the connection is bound to it. Failed logins are rate-limited per user.
post.summary: Check a user's password and open a session of 12 hours; the connection is bound to it.

post.description: End the session this connection is bound to.
post.summary: End the session this connection is bound to.

post.description: Remove a user and end its sessions.
post.summary: Remove a user and end its sessions.

post.description: Revoke an API token at once.
post.summary: Revoke an API token at once.

post.description: Add a user, or change its role or password (a crypt(3) hash; `!` locks it, empty keeps it). Ends the user's sessions.
post.summary: Add a user, or change its role or password (a crypt(3) hash; `!` locks it, empty keeps it).

post.description: Move a pair's gateway addresses to `to` (default: the node with the higher VRRP priority). Returns when the move is done, or why it did not happen.

master.description: The node that holds the gateway addresses now.

post.summary: Move a pair's gateway addresses to `to` (default: the node with the higher VRRP priority).

post.description: Capture packets on `network` as a pcap (#265), matching `filter` (pcap-filter syntax), for `seconds` (default 30, at most 300) or until `max_size` bytes (default 8 MiB, at most 32 MiB), whichever comes first. With `more`, the pcap's bytes as they come; without, all of it in one reply. One capture runs on a node at a time, and each is recorded in the journal.

parameters.description: Stream replies as an RFC 7464 JSON text sequence (application/json-seq) until the connection closes.
parameters.name: more

bytes.description: The capture's size so far, in bytes.

data.description: The next of the pcap's bytes, in base64: empty in the last reply of a stream.

end.description: Why it ended, in the last reply: `time` (its time limit), `size` (its size limit; the packet past it is left out) or `stopped` (tcpdump stopped, the interface gone, say).
